newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Gunmen kill four in S.Africa's Zulu province.
newsitem.headline: Gunmen kill four in S.Africa's Zulu province.

text.p: Gunmen shot dead four people in an ambush on Monday in South Africa's troubled KwaZulu-Natal province, police said.
About 30 men armed with automatic assault rifles and handguns ambushed a minibus taxi carrying 10 people near Greytown in central KwaZulu-Natal, a police spokesman said.
"Two people were shot dead inside the taxi and a pedestrian was killed as well," Inspector Gerry Brits told Reuters.
The gunmen then ran into a nearby forest where they shot dead one man and seriously wounded another, he added.
The killings appeared to be related to a feud between two black clans living in the area which was sparked by an argument between their chiefs about two years ago, Brits said.
"It is too early to say if this taxi was attacked for a specific reason or if it was just in the wrong place at the wrong time," he said.
The province has a history of violence, much of it political conflict between President Nelson Mandela's African National Congress and the Zulu-traditionalist Inkatha Freedom Party.
